title: Payments platform on Kubernetes with a card vault

organisation.name: Corvane Pay
organisation.industry: Fintech: online card payments for merchants
organisation.size: 340 staff; platform, payments and data science teams
organisation.summary: Corvane Pay processes card payments for about 2,000 online merchants. Merchant servers call a partner API through a gateway that requires mutual TLS; the payments API runs as pods on a managed Kubernetes cluster, scores every payment with an in-house fraud model and publishes events that a settlement worker turns into payouts. Card numbers live only in a card vault in a separate data account, encrypted with a dedicated key. Merchants also submit chargeback labels that retrain the fraud model weekly. Deployments run from CI with OIDC federation to a cloud deploy role, and security logs flow into a SIEM in a security account.

attackerOrigins.label: malicious merchant account
attackerOrigins.detail: A real merchant account with a valid certificate, used for fraud

identities.label: merchant client certificates and tokens
privileges: call the payments API as one merchant
identities.notes: The certificate says which merchant is calling; OAuth scopes say which endpoints it may use

privileges: write to the chargeback labels bucket

controls.label: mTLS
controls.covers: Only merchants with a valid client certificate reach the API
controls.limits: Proves which merchant is calling, not which merchant's payments it may touch

controls.label: rate limits
controls.covers: Per-merchant request rates on the partner API
controls.limits: Generous for scoring calls, so slow probing stays under them

controls.label: OAuth scopes
controls.covers: Which endpoints a merchant token may call
controls.limits: The refunds and labels endpoints accept any token with the payments scope and do not check ownership of the payment id

controls.label: tokenisation
controls.covers: Card numbers never leave the vault except for refunds to card
controls.limits: Any workload holding the settlement role can detokenise

controls.label: key policy
controls.covers: Only the vault and the settlement role may decrypt

controls.label: OIDC to cloud
controls.covers: No long-lived cloud keys in CI
controls.limits: The deploy role trusts tokens from every branch, not only protected main

controls.label: phishing-resistant MFA
controls.covers: Engineer sign-in to CI and the cluster
controls.limits: Does not protect a session cookie that is already issued

controls.label: card-data alerts
controls.covers: Alerts on detokenise and decrypt calls by unexpected identities
controls.limits: Sees gateway and key logs only; no Kubernetes audit events

controls.label: network policies
controls.covers: Limiting which pods may talk to each other in the cluster

controls.label: label validation
controls.covers: Checking merchant-submitted labels before they retrain the model

trustRelationships.via: OIDC federation: the role trusts the repository's workflow tokens
trustRelationships.notes: Any branch can request the role

trustRelationships.via: cross-account read role for vault backups
trustRelationships.notes: Kept from a migration last year

trustRelationships.via: flat pod network: any pod can reach the settlement worker
trustRelationships.notes: The worker's internal endpoint has no authentication

cloud_security.summary: A workflow on an unprotected branch exchanges its OIDC token for the deploy role
The deploy role's leftover cross-account read role reaches the card vault backups

api_security.summary: The refunds endpoint accepts another merchant's payment id with any valid token
A merchant's client certificate and token are taken from its server and replayed

data_security.summary: A compromised pod reaches the settlement worker, which can detokenise any card
Chargeback labels with payment ids are readable by every workload with the payments role

devsecops_supply_chain.summary: A pull request edits the workflow so its own branch deploys with the deploy role
A tampered base image is built and deployed to the payments pods

container_kubernetes.summary: A compromised payments pod reaches the settlement worker across a flat pod network
The deploy role can create any workload, including one that runs as the settlement service account

identity_access.summary: An engineer's SSO session cookie is stolen and replayed against CI
The deploy role trusts workflow tokens from every branch, not only main

grc_risk.summary: The flat pod network puts every cluster workload in PCI scope
Merchant-submitted labels retrain the fraud model with no review

security_operations.summary: The SIEM alerts on detokenise calls by an identity that never made them before
A deploy from a feature branch is visible only in CI history, not in the SIEM

zero_trust.summary: A valid merchant certificate is treated as permission to act for any merchant
Any pod in the cluster is trusted to call the settlement worker

ai_llm_security.summary: A merchant uploads crafted chargeback labels that teach the fraud model to pass its own fraud
Repeated scoring requests map the fraud model's thresholds

reviewNotes: Intermediate: two paths that look safe because of a control (mTLS, OIDC) but are not (ownership not checked; every branch trusted). Pod network is flat; the SIEM sees no cluster or CI events.
